{{Short description|Theorem in complex analysis}}
'''Mergelyan's theorem''' is a result from approximation by polynomials in  [[complex analysis]] proved by the [[Armenian SSR|Armenian]] [[mathematician]] [[Sergey Mergelyan|Sergei Mergelyan]] in 1951. 

== Statement ==
:Let <math>K</math> be a [[compact set|compact subset]] of the [[complex plane]] <math>\mathbb C</math> such that <math>\mathbb C \setminus K</math> is [[connected set|connected]]. Then, every [[continuous function]] <math>f : K\to \mathbb C</math>, such that the [[Restriction (mathematics)|restriction]] <math>f</math> to <math>\text{int}(K)</math> is [[holomorphic function|holomorphic]], can be approximated [[uniform convergence|uniformly]] on <math>K</math> with [[polynomial]]s. Here, <math>\text{int}(K)</math> denotes the [[interior_(topology)|interior]] of <math>K</math>.<ref name=A>{{cite journal
 | last = Forstnerič | first = Franc
 | arxiv = 1801.04773
 | doi = 10.17323/1609-4514-2019-19-3-465-484
 | issue = 3
 | journal = Moscow Mathematical Journal
 | mr = 3993004
 | pages = 465–484
 | title = Mergelyan's and Arakelian's theorems for manifold-valued maps
 | volume = 19
 | year = 2019}}</ref><ref name=B>{{cite book |first1=J.E.|last1 =Fornaess |last2=Forstneric |first2=F |last3=Wold |first3=E.F |editor1-first=Daniel |editor1-last=Breaz |editor2-first=Michael Th. |editor2-last=Rassias |title=Advancements in Complex Analysis – Holomorphic Approximation |chapter=The Legacy of Weierstrass, Runge, Oka–Weil, and Mergelyan |date=2020 |publisher=[[Springer Nature]] |pages=133–192|doi=10.1007/978-3-030-40120-7|arxiv=1802.03924 |isbn =978-3-030-40119-1 |s2cid =220266044 }}</ref>

Mergelyan's theorem also holds for open [[Riemann surfaces]]. Let <math>\mathcal{A} (K)</math> be set of all continuous and complex-valued functions in <math>\text{int}(K)</math>, and  <math>\mathcal{O}(X)</math> be the set of all functions that are holomorphic in a neighborhood of <math>K</math>. Then:

:If <math>K</math> is a compact set without holes in an open [[Riemann surface]] <math>X</math>, then every function in <math>\mathcal{A} (K)</math> can be approximated uniformly on <math>K</math> by functions in <math>\mathcal{O}(X)</math>.{{R|B}}

Mergelyan's theorem does not always hold in higher dimensions (spaces of [[several complex variables]]), but it has some consequences.{{R|B}}

== History ==

Mergelyan's theorem is a generalization of the [[Weierstrass approximation theorem]] and [[Runge's theorem]].

In the case that <math>\mathbb C\setminus K</math> is ''not'' connected, in the initial approximation problem the polynomials have to be replaced by [[rational function]]s. An important step of the solution of this further [[Padé approximant|rational approximation]] problem was also suggested by Mergelyan in 1952. Further deep results on rational approximation are due to, in particular, [[A. G. Vitushkin]].

Weierstrass and Runge's theorems were put forward in 1885, while Mergelyan's theorem dates from 1951. After Weierstrass and Runge, many mathematicians (in particular [[Joseph Leonard Walsh|Walsh]], [[Mstislav Keldysh|Keldysh]], [[Mikhail Lavrentyev|Lavrentyev]], [[Friedrich Hartogs|Hartogs]], and [[Arthur Rosenthal|Rosenthal]]) had been working on the same problem. The method of the proof suggested by Mergelyan is constructive, and remains the only known constructive proof of the result.{{Citation needed|date=July 2021}}
